moments.title: "The number of years with the compounding just multiplies your money"
moments.summary: A participant, mid-answer as the recording starts, names time and compounding as the thing that amazed her.
moments.evidence: That's like number of years with the compounding just multiplies your money and how. That was amazing.

moments.title: She now wakes up with 100 questions about ETFs and equities for her husband
moments.summary: A participant says she had no interest in reading the Economic Times before; now she questions her husband every morning, he is impressed, and he is more interested in talking to her about it.
moments.evidence: I think I had no interest in reading the economic times or knowing what the market was about and now every morning I wake up and I have 100 questions for him

moments.title: She opened 20 years of insurance and financial papers and started questioning her accountant
moments.summary: Another participant describes going to her office, opening all the insurance and financial documents, and asking her accountant so many questions that he remarked she had never come in 20 years.
moments.evidence: I have gone to my office, opened all the insurance papers and all the financial documents and I'm asking so many questions to my accountant.

moments.title: Investing with understanding instead of blindly following someone
moments.summary: Asked whether she feels more in control of her money, a participant says the difference is investing with an understanding rather than blindly doing it or following what somebody tells her.
moments.evidence: the understanding of how smartly and efficiently I can invest my money with an understanding, not blindly doing it or following somebody telling me,

moments.title: She can now counter-question her financial planner
moments.summary: A participant says that even sitting with her financial planner she will now understand what he is explaining and can counter-question him about it.
moments.evidence: Even if I'm sitting with my financial planner, at least I'll have an understanding of what he's talking to me and what he's explaining to me, I can counter question him about the stuff he's talking to me.

moments.title: The class gave her an interest in the subject first, confidence second
moments.summary: A participant says the biggest change was developing an interest in the subject, and that her confidence and understanding followed from the class being interesting.
moments.evidence: I think for me, it has helped me develop an interest in the subject first. And obviously now I'm more confident and the understanding has increased,

moments.title: Planning the portfolio, not just investing for the sake of investing
moments.summary: Asked what she will do differently, an already-investing participant names long term planning — planning her portfolio rather than investing for its own sake — and says she will sit with her family to review how well they have planned.
moments.evidence: I think what I'm going to do differently is going through long term planning because you've made me understand planning not just for investing, for the sake of investing and understanding my portfolio, but planning my portfolio.

moments.title: The most fun part was the games, especially the stock market one
moments.summary: Asked for the most fun part of the session, the table answers the games immediately and singles out the stock market game.
moments.evidence: The games. The games were just fantastic. Especially the stock market.
